_meta.source_document: District Environmental Plan for Bengaluru Urban District, Karnataka State
_meta.data_as_on: Base data from 'Bengaluru Urban District at a Glance 2019-2020' (Govt. of Karnataka); KSPCB F-Register / industry status current to ~2021-22; action-plan timelines run 31.12.2021 to 31.03.2023. Cited throughout as 'DEP 2022' with the 2019-20 base year noted.
_meta.extraction_method: pdftotext -layout on machine-readable (text-based) PDF; cover page rendered empty, all data pages selectable text.
_meta.structure_note: This DEP is organised PER ULB (BBMP, TMC-Anekal, TMC-Attibele, TMC-Bommasandra, TMC-Chandapura, CMC-Hebbagodi, TMC-Jigani), NOT per valley. There is no per-valley (V-Valley / K&C-Valley) data table in the document. The only Arkavathi-basin urban unit is BBMP (city corporation), whose west and south drain via the Vrishabhavathi (V-Valley), a tributary of the Arkavathi. The six small TMCs/CMC of Anekal taluk lie in the K&C Valley / Dakshina Pinakini (Pennar) catchment, not the Arkavathi.
_meta.v_valley_row_caveat: The exact '144 industries (Red-29, Orange-43, Green-72) ... 3515 KLD sewage and 4715 KLD trade effluent ... 19 STPs and 31 ETPs ... 250 KLD CETP proposed in Peenya' row cited in the task does NOT appear verbatim in this Bengaluru Urban DEP. That valley-resolution row is from a different source (NMCG MPR / V-Valley NGT documentation), not this district DEP. This DEP instead carries DISTRICT-WIDE KSPCB industry counts (Red 1025 / Orange 2268 / Green 5441 / White 981) and 4 Common Effluent Treatment Facilities, plus per-ULB sewage/STP tables. The Peenya 250 KLD CETP is NOT mentioned here as a proposal; Peenya appears only as a 'Critically Polluted Area' (CEPI 78.12) with NGT OA 1038/2018 groundwater-remediation directions. All figures below are verbatim from this DEP only.
_meta.internal_inconsistency_caveat: The DEP's own tables disagree on BBMP sewage generation: the at-a-glance Water Quality table prints 1440 MLD, the STP-adequacy gap table prints 1440 MLD generated, but the section header 'Total sewage' line and the per-ULB total print 1458.6 MLD (district) and 1457.6 MLD (gap-table district total). Both are reproduced verbatim in sources.

bbmp.name: BBMP (Bengaluru city corporation; west/south = V-Valley / Vrishabhavathi)
bbmp.coverage: Bengaluru Urban DEP 2022 (base data 'District at a Glance 2019-20')
bbmp.headline: City sewage runs close to installed STP capacity on paper, but ~20% has no sewer network and the V-Valley's Peenya cluster is a CPCB Critically Polluted Area with chromium-contaminated groundwater

streams.summary: BBMP shows ~1440 MLD generated vs 1522.5 MLD installed STP capacity and only ~1050 MLD actual flow treated; the DEP records a 0 MLD capacity 'gap' but a 20% sewer-network gap (8-10% of sewage untreated)

metrics.label: Capacity-vs-generation gap (BBMP)
metrics.value: 0 MLD on paper; district gap 15.35 MLD (DEP 2022)

metrics.label: Sewer-network gap (BBMP)
metrics.value: 20% of UGD area uncovered; 8-10% of sewage untreated (DEP 2022)

metrics.label: Untreated-sewage fix plan
metrics.value: 124 MLD via 14 WWTPs + UGD to 110 villages, by 2024 (DEP 2022)

metrics.label: STP compliance
metrics.value: Not tabulated per-STP in this DEP; KSPCB monitors WQ of 165 lakes (DEP 2022)

sources.says: There are 07 Local bodies in the District. BBMP, TMC-Anekal have provided STPs... there is a gap in sewer network in BBMP area, which results in 8 to 10% of sewage is untreated. This gap shall be fulfilled by 2024 after completion of providing UGD facilities to 110 villages of BBMP and construction of 14 Nos. of Waste Water Treatment Plants of total 124 MLD capacity.

sources.citation: District Environmental Plan for Bengaluru Urban District, p.87 and p.91

streams.summary: District-wide 25.34 MLD trade effluent from 2018 discharging industries, all reported treated in-premises with 4 Common Effluent Treatment Facilities; Peenya cluster (V-Valley) is a CPCB Critically Polluted Area with chromium-contaminated groundwater under NGT OA 1038/2018

metrics.label: Peenya cluster (V-Valley) status
metrics.value: CPCB Critically Polluted Area, CEPI 78.12; groundwater Cr/nitrate/hardness contaminated; NGT Suo Moto OA 1038/2018 (DEP 2022)

sources.source: Bengaluru Urban DEP 2022 - Industrial Wastewater Management current status (p.93)
sources.says: Nos. of Red industries: 1025; Orange: 2268; Green: 5441; White: 981. No of Industries discharging wastewater: 2018. Total Quantity of industrial waste water generated: 25.34 MLD. Quantity of treated industrial waste water discharged in to Nalas/Rivers: NIL. Common Effluent Treatment Facilities: 4. No of Industries meeting Standards: 1178. No of Industries not meeting discharge Standards: 27.
sources.citation: District Environmental Plan for Bengaluru Urban District, Industrial Wastewater Management, p.93

sources.says: About 25.31 MLD of wastewater is being generated from the industries, which is being treated in the treatment plants provided by the industries to the standards prescribed by the KSPCB and treated water is used for washing, recycling and on land for gardening within their premises.
sources.citation: District Environmental Plan for Bengaluru Urban District, p.78

sources.source: Bengaluru Urban DEP 2022 - Water Quality / groundwater section (p.79, p.~84)
sources.says: Peenya Industrial Cluster is notified as 'Critically Polluted Area' with CEPI score of 78.12 as per CPCB. The underground water of Peenya Industrial Cluster is contaminated with Chromium, Nitrates and Hardness. Hon'ble NGT registered the Suo Moto in OA No.1038/2018. Short and Long term action plan w.r.t. remediation of ground water pollution at Peenya cluster is submitted to NGT through CPCB.
sources.citation: District Environmental Plan for Bengaluru Urban District, Water Quality Management, p.79 and p.~84
